content:
Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt joined a burgeoning chorus of concerned American citizens asking President Donald Trump and his administration to be “transparent” about recent tech outages following last week’s nationwide flight shutdown.

“I am one of those Americans now, right?” Leavitt told “Fox & Friends” host Ainsley Earhardt on Tuesday. “No longer serving in government, no longer getting those classified briefings about what’s really going on behind the scenes. So as I’m here raising my family, I’m wondering the same thing: What’s happening?”

Leavitt, who resigned as White House press secretary earlier this year, was referring to a slew of unnerving tech issues that occurred over the past few days that have affected companies such as Microsoft, and major U.S. banks, including Wells Fargo, Chase and Bank of America.

“I’m checking my bank account with a little bit of worry,” Leavitt admitted.

She continued, “And what I would say to the White House is, transparency is key. It’s going to help the country grapple with what’s going on. I saw the vice president in his interview with Laura Ingraham last night saying, ‘We don’t see a crisis coming.’”

Vice President JD Vance indeed told the Fox News host on Monday that the U.S. government isn’t aware of any serious and impending crises, fears of which first emerged in earnest when the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a four-hour nationwide flight shutdown on Friday.

Rumors of a nationwide blackout have been spreading on social media for weeks, however, bolstered by the fact that several countries have advised their populations to stock up on water and canned food in case the power grid goes down for a few days — or more.

Leavitt on Tuesday urged the White House to take Vance’s rosier message “wide and loud” if there is indeed no cause for concern, and acknowledged that Trump himself is currently in the Philippines on the first leg of his official trip to Asia for the ASEAN-U.S. Summit.

“I think when he returns home, there should be a message directly to the American people, whether it’s from him or somebody else at the White House, saying what they know and what they believe to be true, to really calm the temperature,” Leavitt told Earhardt.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin have attributed last week’s flight shutdown to issues with old FAA equipment, but banking issues following in such quick succession have nonetheless left many Americans concerned.

CNN reported Tuesday that an internal network used by NSA employees to communicate classified information was down, and news of a nationwide Emergency Alert System test being scheduled for 2:20 p.m. ET has further alarmed skeptics and conspiracy theorists.

While that segment of the population has perhaps understandably filled a void of lacking answers from the Trump administration with predictions of their own, it appears each outage and issue was independent from one another — and likely caused by a temporary bug.

“I’ve noticed this whole situation has really taken off on TikTok,” Leavitt told Earhardt.

She concluded, “A lot of my friends back home have been asking, ‘What’s going on?’ — for weeks now. So this has really been spiraling for quite some time and I think, again, the White House should just address it directly with the American people.”
